Plain-language start for DOTE5891. Definitions stay in the [Glossary](glossary.qmd); citeable status stays on [Official status](tracker.qmd).

## A whole service, not only a vehicle

In Hong Kong, **low-altitude economy (LAE)** means economic activity in airspace generally below about **1,000 metres** — a **policy working description**, not a Cap. 448G flying limit ([Glossary · altitude scale](glossary.qmd#altitude-scale); [Official status](tracker.qmd)).

Picture a completed mission: someone needs a delivery, inspection, medical transfer, or similar job done. An **operator** flies (or manages) the aircraft; the craft needs somewhere to take off and land; someone coordinates traffic and communications; **customers or mission sponsors** pay for the outcome; and supporting services (finance, insurance, training, platforms) keep the operation going. That whole chain is what the course means by LAE — Week 1 on [Lectures](lectures.qmd) opens the same idea; the week map is on [Course overview](overview.qmd).

Mainland **低空经济** uses a separate statistical / industrial-policy scope (NDRC 发改低空〔2025〕1676号). Do not treat it as the same metric as a Hong Kong value-added figure ([Glossary](glossary.qmd#mainland-comparators); [Official status](tracker.qmd)).

## Labels you will meet (keep light)

You will hear everyday words (“drone”) and law or industry labels side by side. Hong Kong’s main legal label for light unmanned craft is **small unmanned aircraft (SUA)** under [Cap. 448G](glossary.qmd#hong-kong-institutions-and-law) (not more than **150 kg**). **eVTOL** is an industry label for electric vertical take-off and landing craft; Hong Kong has **no dedicated eVTOL statute yet**, and heavier / passenger types sit above the SUA ceiling as **unconventional aircraft** pending rules ([Glossary · vehicles](glossary.qmd#vehicles-and-operations); [Official status](tracker.qmd)).

```{=html}
<div class="plab-grid">

<div class="plab-box"><span class="tag">SUA</span><strong>Small unmanned aircraft</strong>Hong Kong Cap. 448G term for unmanned aircraft not more than <strong>150 kg</strong>. “Drone” in everyday speech is not a Cap. 448G synonym. <a href="glossary.qmd#hong-kong-institutions-and-law">Cap. 448G</a> · <a href="glossary.qmd#vehicles-and-operations">vehicles</a></div>

</div>
<p class="plab-note">Sites (vertiports), U-space / UTM, BVLOS, and permission ladders: see prose below and Glossary diagrams — not reprinted here.</p>

```

Sites for advanced craft are often called **vertiports** in industry language — again, **no dedicated Hong Kong vertiport statute yet** ([Glossary · infrastructure](glossary.qmd#infrastructure)). Traffic labels such as **U-space** (EU / industry, **not Hong Kong law**) and **UTM** (industry usage) appear in readings; Hong Kong’s Smart Low-altitude Traffic Management System is **planned** (Policy Address language: progressive implementation from **2028**), not yet a statute ([Glossary · airspace](glossary.qmd#airspace-and-traffic); [Timeline](dates.qmd)). Weight ladders, BVLOS, and permission diagrams live on the Glossary — this page does not reprint them.

## Why Hong Kong and the GBA

The course centres Hong Kong and the Greater Bay Area, with EU / US / NASA-style comparators on [Course overview](overview.qmd) and [Readings](readings.qmd). Hong Kong already has an active policy track (Working Group, sandboxes, Cap. 448G and Advisory Circulars) on [Timeline](dates.qmd).
